title: Deep pipeline for high clock rate
decision: Design an even deeper pipeline (about two times the P6 microarchitecture) with fewer gates of logic per clock cycle
alternatives_or_rejected: Shallower pipelines comparable to P6 / prior Intel pipelines that would yield lower frequency on the same process
rationale: The final frequency depends heavily on how deeply the processor is pipelined; deeper pipelining with fewer gates per stage enables industry-leading clock rates
outcome: Pentium 4 targeted greater than 1.6 times higher frequency than P6 family on the same process; 20-stage misprediction pipeline versus P6's 10-stage
quote_as_recalled: The NetBurst microarchitecture was designed to have an even deeper pipeline (about two times the P6 microarchitecture)
weakest_point: Exact page number within the journal issue

title: Execution Trace Cache instead of conventional L1I
decision: Replace a conventional instruction cache with an Execution Trace Cache that stores already-decoded uops and sits between the decoders and the execution core
alternatives_or_rejected: Conventional instruction cache that stores raw IA-32 instruction bytes (requiring decode on every fetch from the L1I)
rationale: IA-32 instructions are cumbersome to decode (variable length, many options); storing already-decoded uops removes decoding from the main execution loop and supplies high bandwidth to the out-of-order core
outcome: Trace Cache holds up to 12K uops, delivers up to three uops per clock, has hit rate similar to an 8K-16K byte conventional I-cache; most instructions execute from the Trace Cache
quote_as_recalled: Unlike conventional instruction caches, the Trace Cache sits between the instruction decode logic and the execution core
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly quantifies decode complexity as the primary rejected alternative motivation

title: Double-pumped (2x) ALUs for low-latency integer execution
where_in_paper: Execution units / Rapid Execution Engine discussion
decision: Run the simple integer ALUs at twice the core clock frequency (double-pumped) so that basic ALU operations have very low effective latency
rationale: Enable high throughput and low latency for the most common integer operations while the rest of the machine runs at the main clock rate
outcome: ALUs can start a new operation every half-cycle of the main clock; staggered add makes the lower half of the result available early to dependent operations
quote_as_recalled: extremely low latency double-pumped Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
weakest_point: Precise wording of the staggered-add description may be slightly off

title: Small low-latency L1 data cache backed by large L2
where_in_paper: Memory subsystem / L1 data cache discussion
decision: Use a small, very low-latency 8 KB L1 data cache optimized for lowest overall load-access latency, backed by a large high-bandwidth L2
rationale: Optimize for the lowest overall load-access latency; for most IA-32 programs a small very-low-latency L1 followed by a large medium-latency L2 is effective
outcome: L1 data cache accessed in two clock cycles; configuration described as giving good overall latency characteristics
quote_as_recalled: optimizes for the lowest overall load-access latency with a small, very low latency 8K byte cache
weakest_point: Exact size and cycle count wording may blend with general P4 knowledge

title: Deeper buffering for out-of-order window
decision: Provide much deeper buffering than the P6 microarchitecture (up to 126 instructions in flight, 48 loads, 24 stores)
alternatives_or_rejected: P6-scale buffering that limits the number of in-flight instructions
rationale: By looking at a larger number of instructions at once the out-of-order engine can usually find more ready-to-execute independent instructions each cycle
outcome: Machine can have up to 126 instructions in flight and allocate up to 48 loads and 24 stores simultaneously
quote_as_recalled: The NetBurst microarchitecture has much deeper buffering than the P6 microarchitecture to allow this.
weakest_point: Exact buffer counts may be recalled with slight error
